content: 1. Khatana GH, Haq I, Khan SMS conducted a study in Kashmir to evaluate the effectiveness, acceptance, and feasibility of a home-based intervention model for tuberculosis contact tracing. The findings were published in the Journal of Clinical Tuberculosis and Other Mycobacterial Diseases in 2019. 2. Kigozi NG, Heunis JC, and Engelbrecht MC investigated the yield of systematic household contact investigation for tuberculosis in a high-burden metropolitan district of South Africa. Their results were published in BMC Public Health in 2019. 3. Kliner M, Knight A, Elston J, and colleagues developed and tested models for tuberculosis contact tracing in rural southern Africa. Their work was published in Public Health Action in 2013. 4. Laghari M, Sulaiman SAS, Khan AH, and colleagues explored contact screening and risk factors for tuberculosis among household contacts of children with active TB. They aimed to identify source cases and new TB cases, with findings published in BMC Public Health in 2019. 5. Lala SG, Little KM, Tshabangu N, and colleagues conducted an observational study on integrated source case investigation for tuberculosis and HIV in caregivers and household contacts of hospitalized young children diagnosed with TB in South Africa. The study was published in PLoS One in 2015. 6. Lebina L, Fuller N, Osoba T, and colleagues assessed the use of Xpert MTB/Rif for active case finding among TB contacts in North West Province, South Africa. Their findings were published in Tuberculosis Research and Treatment in 2016. 7. Little KM, Msandiwa R, Martinson N, and colleagues evaluated the yield of household contact tracing for tuberculosis in rural South Africa. Their study was published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2018. 8. Lopez-Varela E, Augusto OJ, Gondo K, and colleagues studied the incidence of tuberculosis among young children in rural Mozambique. Their findings were published in the Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal in 2015. 9. Mandalakas AM, Ngo K, Alonso Ustero P, and colleagues implemented the BUTIMBA project in Swaziland, intensifying the hunt for child TB through household contact tracing. The study was published in PLoS One in 2017. 10. Martinez L, Handel A, Shen Y, and colleagues conducted a prospective validation of a clinical algorithm to detect tuberculosis in child contacts. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine in 2018. 11. Martinez L, Sekandi JN, Castellanos ME, and colleagues examined the infectiousness of HIV-seropositive patients with tuberculosis in a high-burden African setting. Their study was published in the American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine in 2016. 12. Martinez L, Shen Y, Handel A, and colleagues evaluated the effectiveness of the WHO’s pragmatic screening algorithm for child contacts of tuberculosis cases in resource-constrained settings. Their prospective cohort study in Uganda was published in The Lancet Respiratory Medicine in 2018. 13. Masur J, Koenig SP, Julma P, and colleagues conducted active tuberculosis case finding in Haiti. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2017. 14. Mazahir R, Beig FK, Ahmed Z, and colleagues assessed the burden of tuberculosis among household children of adult multidrug-resistant patients and their response to first-line anti-tubercular drugs. Their study was published in the Egyptian Pediatric Association Gazette in 2017. 15. Moore HA, Apolles P, De Villiers PJT, and colleagues evaluated sputum induction for microbiological diagnosis of childhood pulmonary tuberculosis in a community setting. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2011. 16. Muyoyeta M, Kasese NC, Milimo D, and colleagues compared digital chest X-rays with computer-aided diagnosis versus symptom screening to define presumptive tuberculosis among household contacts. Their study was published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2017. 17. Mwanza-Kambafwile J, McCarthy K, Gharbaharan V, and colleagues evaluated a paper slip method for tuberculosis case finding and contact tracing. Their findings were published in PLoS One in 2013. 18. Nair D, Rajshekhar N, Klinton JS, and colleagues conducted a clinic-based study on household contact screening and tuberculosis case yield in Chennai, South India. Their study was published in PLoS One in 2016. 19. Ntinginya NE, Squire SB, Millington KA, and colleagues assessed the performance of the Xpert MTB/RIF assay in an active case-finding strategy in Tanzania. Their pilot study was published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2012. 20. Ohene SA, Bonsu F, Hanson-Nortey NN, and colleagues investigated the yield of tuberculosis among household contacts of TB patients in Accra, Ghana. Their findings were published in Infectious Diseases of Poverty in 2018.
